game_changers: Tergrid, God of Fright // Tergrid's Lantern

1.name: Exhibition
1.summary: Ultra-casual. The deck exists to show off a theme or a joke, not to win. Games go long and everyone gets to do their thing.
rules: No Game Changers.
No mass land denial.
No chaining extra turns.
No two-card infinite combos.
Games are expected to go long; winning is not the point.

2.name: Core
2.summary: Precon-level. The baseline Commander experience -- a modern preconstructed deck out of the box lands here.
rules: No Game Changers.
No mass land denial.
No chaining extra turns.
No two-card infinite combos.
Power level of a modern precon; games typically end around turn 9 or later.

3.name: Upgraded
3.summary: A precon that has been deliberately tuned, or a deck built to beat one. Stronger cards and tighter curve, still not cutthroat.
rules: Up to 3 Game Changers.
No mass land denial.
No chaining extra turns.
Late-game two-card infinite combos are tolerated.
Noticeably stronger than a precon; games typically end around turn 7 or later.

4.name: Optimized
4.summary: High power. The strongest version of the deck you want to play, built without deck-construction restrictions but not aimed at a tournament metagame.
rules: No restrictions: any number of Game Changers.
Mass land denial, extra-turn chains and two-card infinite combos are all allowed.
Built to be as strong as possible within its own strategy.
Not tuned for a competitive metagame -- that is Bracket 5.

5.name: cEDH
5.summary: Competitive EDH. Tournament-tuned and metagame-driven: every card is chosen to win, and to win as fast as possible.
rules: No restrictions: any number of Game Changers.
Deckbuilding is driven by the competitive metagame, not by the pilot's preference.
Wins as fast as possible; free interaction and fast mana are expected.
Only the banned list constrains construction.
